from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
print("size:", im.size)

# Per-column mean color
col = a.mean(axis=0)  # (W, 3)
W = col.shape[0]
print("W =", W)

# Detect stripe boundaries: columns where color changes significantly
diff = np.abs(np.diff(col, axis=0)).sum(axis=1)
print("max col diff:", diff.max(), "mean:", diff.mean())

# Find contiguous runs of similar color (stripes)
import colorsys
def rgb2hex(c):
    return '#%02x%02x%02x' % tuple(int(round(x)) for x in c)

# Simple segmentation: boundaries where diff > threshold
th = max(8, np.percentile(diff, 90))
bounds = [0] + [i+1 for i in range(W-1) if diff[i] > th] + [W]
# merge tiny segments
segs = [(bounds[i], bounds[i+1]) for i in range(len(bounds)-1)]
merged = []
for s,e in segs:
    if merged and (e-s) < 2:
        merged[-1] = (merged[-1][0], e)
    else:
        merged.append((s,e))
print("num segments:", len(merged))
widths = [e-s for s,e in merged]
print("widths:", widths)
print("median width:", np.median(widths))
EOF

"**Propuesta Indecente**" ("Indecent Proposal") is a [bachata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachata_\(music\) "Bachata (music)") song by American singer [Romeo Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo_Santos "Romeo Santos"), released on July 30, 2013 as the lead single from his second studio album *[Formula, Vol. 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula,_Vol._2 "Formula, Vol. 2")*. It became one of the best-performing songs in Latin music. The song mixes the sound of Dominican bachata and Argentinian [tango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tango "Tango").

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Composition")\]

Written by Santos himself, "Propuesta Indecente" is a Dominican [bachata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachata_\(music\) "Bachata (music)") song, with incorporations of Argentinian [tango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tango "Tango").[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

In January 2017, it was certified double-diamond [in the Latin field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification#Latin "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") for selling over 1\.2 million units in the United States.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) It also became the first song to remain on the US [Hot Latin Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs") chart for over 100 weeks.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) As of 2021[\[update\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit), "Propuesta Indecente" is the second best performing Latin song ever on the *Billboard* Hot Latin Songs chart following "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")".[\[5\]](#cite_note-alltime-5)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Music video")\]

Its accompanying music video was released on September 9, 2013, which was filmed at the [National Library of Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Library_of_Argentina "National Library of Argentina") and Palacio San Miguel.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Featuring Mexican entertainer [Eiza González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiza_González "Eiza González"), it begins in a [black-and-white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black-and-white "Black-and-white") scene, with Santos talking to a group of men at a party, eventually making eye contact at González. Throughout the video, surroundings start changing into colors, and both Santos and González begin dancing in the near end of the video and later run outside the palace to a red car, with González spilling a bottle of tequila in front of the palace and lighting the trace on fire before doing so.[\[1\]](#cite_note-:0-1) The video was directed by Joaquín Cambre and produced by Virgin Films.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

The music video attained over 100 million views on social platform [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") in only three months,[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) before attaining over 1 billion views by July 2016,[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) making it the second music video in Spanish and by a Latin artist to do so at the time, behind [Enrique Iglesias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrique_Iglesias "Enrique Iglesias")' "[Bailando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailando_\(Enrique_Iglesias_song\) "Bailando (Enrique Iglesias song)")".[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) It has received over 2\.1 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") as of September 2024\.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

## Accolades

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Accolades")\]

Its music video earned the [Lo Nuestro Award for Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo_Nuestro_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "Lo Nuestro Award for Video of the Year") at the [26th Lo Nuestro Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Lo_Nuestro_2014 "Premio Lo Nuestro 2014"),[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-lonuestro-2014-awards-2-13) with the song itself eventually receiving the [Lo Nuestro Award for Tropical Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo_Nuestro_Award_for_Tropical_Song_of_the_Year "Lo Nuestro Award for Tropical Song of the Year") the [following year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Lo_Nuestro_2015 "Premio Lo Nuestro 2015").[\[14\]](#cite_note-lonuestro-2015-winners-14)

"**Propuesta Indecente**" ("Indecent Proposal") is a [bachata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachata_\(music\) "Bachata (music)") song by American singer [Romeo Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo_Santos "Romeo Santos"), released on July 30, 2013 as the lead single from his second studio album *[Formula, Vol. 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula,_Vol._2 "Formula, Vol. 2")*. It became one of the best-performing songs in Latin music. The song mixes the sound of Dominican bachata and Argentinian [tango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tango "Tango").

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Composition")\]

Written by Santos himself, "Propuesta Indecente" is a Dominican [bachata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachata_\(music\) "Bachata (music)") song, with incorporations of Argentinian [tango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tango "Tango").[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

In January 2017, it was certified double-diamond [in the Latin field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification#Latin "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") for selling over 1\.2 million units in the United States.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) It also became the first song to remain on the US [Hot Latin Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs") chart for over 100 weeks.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) As of 2021[\[update\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit), "Propuesta Indecente" is the second best performing Latin song ever on the *Billboard* Hot Latin Songs chart following "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")".[\[5\]](#cite_note-alltime-5)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Music video")\]

Its accompanying music video was released on September 9, 2013, which was filmed at the [National Library of Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Library_of_Argentina "National Library of Argentina") and Palacio San Miguel.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) Featuring Mexican entertainer [Eiza González](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiza_González "Eiza González"), it begins in a [black-and-white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black-and-white "Black-and-white") scene, with Santos talking to a group of men at a party, eventually making eye contact at González. Throughout the video, surroundings start changing into colors, and both Santos and González begin dancing in the near end of the video and later run outside the palace to a red car, with González spilling a bottle of tequila in front of the palace and lighting the trace on fire before doing so.[\[1\]](#cite_note-:0-1) The video was directed by Joaquín Cambre and produced by Virgin Films.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

The music video attained over 100 million views on social platform [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") in only three months,[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) before attaining over 1 billion views by July 2016,[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) making it the second music video in Spanish and by a Latin artist to do so at the time, behind [Enrique Iglesias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enrique_Iglesias "Enrique Iglesias")' "[Bailando](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailando_\(Enrique_Iglesias_song\) "Bailando (Enrique Iglesias song)")".[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) It has received over 2\.1 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") as of September 2024\.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

## Accolades

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Propuesta_Indecente&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Accolades")\]

Its music video earned the [Lo Nuestro Award for Video of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo_Nuestro_Award_for_Video_of_the_Year "Lo Nuestro Award for Video of the Year") at the [26th Lo Nuestro Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Lo_Nuestro_2014 "Premio Lo Nuestro 2014"),[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-lonuestro-2014-awards-2-13) with the song itself eventually receiving the [Lo Nuestro Award for Tropical Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo_Nuestro_Award_for_Tropical_Song_of_the_Year "Lo Nuestro Award for Tropical Song of the Year") the [following year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premio_Lo_Nuestro_2015 "Premio Lo Nuestro 2015").[\[14\]](#cite_note-lonuestro-2015-winners-14)

"**Criminal**" is a song by Dominican singer [Natti Natasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natti_Natasha "Natti Natasha") and Puerto Rican singer [Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna"), released by [Pina Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pina_Records "Pina Records") on 18 August 2017\. Written by the two singers, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze, it is a [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") genre. The accompanying music video was directed by Nuno Gómes at an abandoned women's prison in [Vega Alta, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Alta,_Puerto_Rico "Vega Alta, Puerto Rico"), and portrays Ozuna as a prison director falling in love with a prisoner played by Natasha. It received over 1 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") within five months of its release and was the most watched music video by a female singer in 2017\.

The track was well received by music critics who found it catchy and praised it for giving reggaeton dance floor appeal. It received a number of award nominations, winning Best Collaboration at the 2018 [Soberano Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soberano_Awards "Soberano Awards"). "Criminal" became a [crossover success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_music "Crossover music") and helped relaunch Natasha's music career, becoming her first top five single on the US [Hot Latin Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs") chart since 2012's "[Dutty Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutty_Love_\(song\) "Dutty Love (song)")" and first chart-topper in Spain where it spent three consecutive weeks at number one. It also topped the charts in El Salvador, Paraguay, Peru and Spain, and reached the top 10 in 10 other Latin American countries.

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

"Criminal" was written by Natasha, Ozuna, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) Pina, Natasha's manager, sent Ozuna the song after two previously failed collaboration attempts, and Ozuna called it a "home run".[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Pina recalled, "After several months of trying to bring up the song, there was always a situation that would have discouraged anybody but, unlike me, I never got up with a 'no' in my head and continued without anything or anyone stopping me."[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Natasha regards "Criminal" as her second chance at a career in music and her first solo release where she had sufficient record label support. Regarding the writing process, she said: "To me, it's such a special song because I had the opportunity to write my part of the lyrics and I just really loved it. When Ozuna agreed, I was extremely excited and for some reason, I knew people were going to love it as much as we did."[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

It is a [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") genre.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music video")\]

[![Ozuna approaching Natti Natasha in an electric chair for a kiss.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/90/Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png/250px-Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png)

Ozuna approaching Natasha in an [electric chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_chair "Electric chair") for a kiss in the music video.

The accompanying music video was directed by Venezuelan director Nuno Gómes. It was filmed at a deactivated women's prison in [Vega Alta, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Alta,_Puerto_Rico "Vega Alta, Puerto Rico") in April 2017 and inspired by the music video for [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga")'s "[Telephone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_\(song\) "Telephone (song)")".[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-Vida_Primo-7) A storm hit Vega Alta a day before the video shoot, resulting in trucks getting stuck in mud and the video wardrobe getting wet. Gómes called it the worst filming day of his career.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6) Filming took nearly 20 hours.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Fashion designer Nelson Tavárez chose bold ensembles for Natasha's wardrobe to portray her character as empowered and confident.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

Natasha plays a prisoner trying to attract the attention of Ozuna, the prison director.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Vida_Primo-7) The clip starts with Natasha being escorted to the prison where Ozuna awaits. They are shown in several locations inside the prison with Natasha performing sensual dances for Ozuna. The video reaches a climax with Natasha sitting in an [electric chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_chair "Electric chair") and Ozuna approaching her for a kiss. Both are struck by electricity, but are shown together amid police alarms in the final scene.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The video led [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube")'s weekly chart for two consecutive weeks in November 2017, ending [Luis Fonsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Fonsi "Luis Fonsi")'s 35-week run at number one with "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")".[\[10\]](#cite_note-Critica-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It surpassed 1 billion views on YouTube within five months of its 18 August 2017 release and was the most watched music video by a female artist in 2017\.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) "Criminal" is one of the 100 most viewed videos and eight most viewed Spanish-language videos on YouTube,[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) having received over 2\.7 billion views as of November 2025\.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Forbes-16) It is also both Natasha and Ozuna's most watched music video on the platform.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Forbes-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) Natasha said YouTube provided her with "the opportunity to reach other parts of the world, when before we depended on a label for that. It's definitely an achievement not only for me, but for Latina women. Before we did not have that reach."[\[10\]](#cite_note-Critica-10) *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* included "Criminal" at number 11 in its list of Top 25 Sexiest Latin Music Videos.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Tommy Calle of *[Hoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoy_\(American_newspaper\) "Hoy (American newspaper)")* wrote that Natasha's "sensuality and beauty" in the video "stands out to the eye".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Hoy_Criminal-19)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

"Criminal" was well received by music critics. [Leila Cobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leila_Cobo "Leila Cobo") of *Billboard* described the song as "sexy without being vulgar" and said its "immediate catchiness" made it "a YouTube sensation".[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) Marjua Esteves of the same website wrote that it is "not your everyday fast-pumping reggaeton record, but a criminally slow-grinding jam".[\[21\]](#cite_note-Billboard-21) Raquel Reichard of *[The Fader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fader "The Fader")* called the track a "knockout" and an "earworm".[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) Writing for *[Maxim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_\(magazine\) "Maxim (magazine)")*, Brandon Friederich found the song "contagious" and wrote, "Even if you're a non-Spanish speaker, just try resisting the urge to sing the 'muy criminal'-laden chorus".[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) [Los 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_40 "Los 40")'s Alberto Palao Murcia commented, "I timidly gave the track a play expecting a more Latin rhythm that does not even reach the dance floor, but, to my surprise, by the second chorus I was already singing 'Criminal, Cri-Criminal..."[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Similarly, Tommy Calle of *Hoy* called it "an urban anthem that has managed to turn on the dance floor",[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) and "a catchy song that lifts everyone's spirits".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Hoy_Criminal-19)

*Billboard* placed "Criminal" at number 17 in its list of Top 20 Best Latin Songs of 2017\.[\[21\]](#cite_note-Billboard-21) [Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")'s Mike Wass gave the song an honorable mention in his list of The Best Latin Pop Songs of 2017\.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)

Language | Spanish

Released | 18 August 2017 (2017-08-18)

["Criminal"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VqEbCxg2bNI) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Criminal**" is a song by Dominican singer [Natti Natasha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natti_Natasha "Natti Natasha") and Puerto Rican singer [Ozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozuna "Ozuna"), released by [Pina Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pina_Records "Pina Records") on 18 August 2017\. Written by the two singers, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze, it is a [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") genre. The accompanying music video was directed by Nuno Gómes at an abandoned women's prison in [Vega Alta, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Alta,_Puerto_Rico "Vega Alta, Puerto Rico"), and portrays Ozuna as a prison director falling in love with a prisoner played by Natasha. It received over 1 billion views on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") within five months of its release and was the most watched music video by a female singer in 2017\.

The track was well received by music critics who found it catchy and praised it for giving reggaeton dance floor appeal. It received a number of award nominations, winning Best Collaboration at the 2018 [Soberano Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soberano_Awards "Soberano Awards"). "Criminal" became a [crossover success](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_music "Crossover music") and helped relaunch Natasha's music career, becoming her first top five single on the US [Hot Latin Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs") chart since 2012's "[Dutty Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutty_Love_\(song\) "Dutty Love (song)")" and first chart-topper in Spain where it spent three consecutive weeks at number one. It also topped the charts in El Salvador, Paraguay, Peru and Spain, and reached the top 10 in 10 other Latin American countries.

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

"Criminal" was written by Natasha, Ozuna, Jhay Cortez, Rafael Pina, Vicente Saavedra and its producer Haze.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) Pina, Natasha's manager, sent Ozuna the song after two previously failed collaboration attempts, and Ozuna called it a "home run".[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Pina recalled, "After several months of trying to bring up the song, there was always a situation that would have discouraged anybody but, unlike me, I never got up with a 'no' in my head and continued without anything or anyone stopping me."[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Natasha regards "Criminal" as her second chance at a career in music and her first solo release where she had sufficient record label support. Regarding the writing process, she said: "To me, it's such a special song because I had the opportunity to write my part of the lyrics and I just really loved it. When Ozuna agreed, I was extremely excited and for some reason, I knew people were going to love it as much as we did."[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

It is a [reggaeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggaeton "Reggaeton") song with drum programming and forceful bass patterns indebted to the [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall") genre.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music video")\]

[![Ozuna approaching Natti Natasha in an electric chair for a kiss.](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/90/Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png/250px-Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Natti_Natasha_-_Criminal_music_video.png)

Ozuna approaching Natasha in an [electric chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_chair "Electric chair") for a kiss in the music video.

The accompanying music video was directed by Venezuelan director Nuno Gómes. It was filmed at a deactivated women's prison in [Vega Alta, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vega_Alta,_Puerto_Rico "Vega Alta, Puerto Rico") in April 2017 and inspired by the music video for [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga")'s "[Telephone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_\(song\) "Telephone (song)")".[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-Vida_Primo-7) A storm hit Vega Alta a day before the video shoot, resulting in trucks getting stuck in mud and the video wardrobe getting wet. Gómes called it the worst filming day of his career.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6) Filming took nearly 20 hours.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Fashion designer Nelson Tavárez chose bold ensembles for Natasha's wardrobe to portray her character as empowered and confident.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

Natasha plays a prisoner trying to attract the attention of Ozuna, the prison director.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Vida_Primo-7) The clip starts with Natasha being escorted to the prison where Ozuna awaits. They are shown in several locations inside the prison with Natasha performing sensual dances for Ozuna. The video reaches a climax with Natasha sitting in an [electric chair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_chair "Electric chair") and Ozuna approaching her for a kiss. Both are struck by electricity, but are shown together amid police alarms in the final scene.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The video led [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube")'s weekly chart for two consecutive weeks in November 2017, ending [Luis Fonsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Fonsi "Luis Fonsi")'s 35-week run at number one with "[Despacito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Despacito "Despacito")".[\[10\]](#cite_note-Critica-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) It surpassed 1 billion views on YouTube within five months of its 18 August 2017 release and was the most watched music video by a female artist in 2017\.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Video-6)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) "Criminal" is one of the 100 most viewed videos and eight most viewed Spanish-language videos on YouTube,[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) having received over 2\.7 billion views as of November 2025\.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Forbes-16) It is also both Natasha and Ozuna's most watched music video on the platform.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Forbes-16)[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) Natasha said YouTube provided her with "the opportunity to reach other parts of the world, when before we depended on a label for that. It's definitely an achievement not only for me, but for Latina women. Before we did not have that reach."[\[10\]](#cite_note-Critica-10) *[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* included "Criminal" at number 11 in its list of Top 25 Sexiest Latin Music Videos.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Tommy Calle of *[Hoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoy_\(American_newspaper\) "Hoy (American newspaper)")* wrote that Natasha's "sensuality and beauty" in the video "stands out to the eye".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Hoy_Criminal-19)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Criminal_\(Natti_Natasha_and_Ozuna_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

"Criminal" was well received by music critics. [Leila Cobo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leila_Cobo "Leila Cobo") of *Billboard* described the song as "sexy without being vulgar" and said its "immediate catchiness" made it "a YouTube sensation".[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) Marjua Esteves of the same website wrote that it is "not your everyday fast-pumping reggaeton record, but a criminally slow-grinding jam".[\[21\]](#cite_note-Billboard-21) Raquel Reichard of *[The Fader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fader "The Fader")* called the track a "knockout" and an "earworm".[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) Writing for *[Maxim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_\(magazine\) "Maxim (magazine)")*, Brandon Friederich found the song "contagious" and wrote, "Even if you're a non-Spanish speaker, just try resisting the urge to sing the 'muy criminal'-laden chorus".[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) [Los 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_40 "Los 40")'s Alberto Palao Murcia commented, "I timidly gave the track a play expecting a more Latin rhythm that does not even reach the dance floor, but, to my surprise, by the second chorus I was already singing 'Criminal, Cri-Criminal..."[\[3\]](#cite_note-Los_40-3) Similarly, Tommy Calle of *Hoy* called it "an urban anthem that has managed to turn on the dance floor",[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) and "a catchy song that lifts everyone's spirits".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Hoy_Criminal-19)

*Billboard* placed "Criminal" at number 17 in its list of Top 20 Best Latin Songs of 2017\.[\[21\]](#cite_note-Billboard-21) [Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")'s Mike Wass gave the song an honorable mention in his list of The Best Latin Pop Songs of 2017\.[\[25\]](#cite_note-25)

import json, numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import colorsys

sb = json.load(open('/tmp/storyboards.json'))

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
col = a.mean(axis=0)  # (1000, 3)
W = col.shape[0]

def rgb2hls_vec(rgb):
    # rgb: (N,3) in 0..255
    c = rgb/255.0
    mx = c.max(axis=1); mn = c.min(axis=1)
    l = (mx+mn)/2
    d = mx-mn
    s = np.where(l<=0, 0, d/(1-np.abs(2*l-1)+1e-12))
    return l, s

results = []
for k, v in sb.items():
    frames = np.array(v['frames'])
    good = ~np.isnan(frames).any(axis=1)
    frames = frames[good]
    dur = v['dur']
    n = len(frames)
    # assume frame i centered at time (i+0.5)*dur/n
    t = (np.arange(n)+0.5) * dur/n
    # resample to W columns
    tc = (np.arange(W)+0.5)/W * dur
    sim = np.zeros((W,3))
    for ch in range(3):
        sim[:,ch] = np.interp(tc, t, frames[:,ch])
    # metrics
    rmse = np.sqrt(((sim-col)**2).mean())
    # cosine similarity per column
    cos = (sim*col).sum(axis=1)/ (np.linalg.norm(sim,axis=1)*np.linalg.norm(col,axis=1)+1e-9)

    corr_l = np.corrcoef(l1,l2)[0,1]
